Title: Passage 1: Making Ice-Cream Memories
Author: by Lissa Rovetch
Content: `text(One day)`, when I arrived at my friend Ollie's house, I found him tossing `text(one)` pebble at a time into a plastic flowerpot. He didn't bother to look at me when I walked up.
“What's going on?” I said...
Ollie sighed. “You know how my grandmother is pretty much like a mom to me?”
I nodded. “Abuela's the best!”
“Well, this `text(year)` I want to do something great for her for Mother's Day,” he said.
“Why do you look so serious about something so fun?” I asked.
“Because I can't think of anything good enough,” he said.
I smiled. “We'll have to go on a sneaky fact-finding mission to figure out what she'd like.”
Right then, Abuela walked outside with a tray of food. “Hello, neighbor!” she said to me. “Won't you join us for lunch? We're having PBBH sandwiches.”
“Thanks! I'd love to,” I replied as we all sat down on the steps. “I know PBJs are peanut butter and jelly, but I've never heard of a PBBH before.”
“It stands for peanut butter, banana, and honey,” she said. “My new specialty.”
“This is delicious!” I said after taking a bite. “Hey, speaking of delicious, what's the most delicious food you've ever eaten, Abuela?” I winked at Ollie.

“Hmm, that's a tricky `text(one)`.” She thought for a `text(minute)`. “Well, nothing beats the wonderful soup Mr. Chan makes at his Happy Garden Restaurant. Except for maybe the soup my grandmother made when I was a girl. And speaking of my grandmother - on certain occasions, she made her special strawberry ice cream. Yep, that homemade ice cream had to be the best thing I've ever tasted!”
Ollie winked at me, smiling for the `text(first)` time since I arrived...
... We had just started our fact-finding mission and had already found a Mother's Day surprise we knew Abuela would love!
Over the next few `text(days)`, Ollie and I asked everyone we knew if they happened to have an old-fashioned ice-cream churn hanging around - but no luck.
So my dad helped us search for some recipes online, and we found a fun one that didn't require any fancy equipment, just a couple of empty coffee cans in different sizes.
My little brother and sister helped us make Mother's Day Ice-Cream Party invitations...
Mother's Day finally arrived, and we were beyond excited to make the ice cream. Sitting outside, we all took turns rolling the can...
... we kept rolling the can while we told stories. We had to roll the can for `text(half an hour)`, but it was so much fun!
When the ice cream was finally ready, Abuela and my mom were the `text(first)` to try it.
“Mmm! Homemade ice cream is even better than I remember!” Abuela smiled from ear to ear.
“I think this is my new favorite Mother's Day tradition!” my mom said, licking her lips.
